title: The Printing Houses
summary: Lyon, spring 2768. The Free Assembly's pamphlets are everywhere, and Lyon's presses print them. The garrison and the city's clergy hunt the presses through the streets before the city turns.

sides.name: The Crown
sides.about: Captain Delorme's garrison, the City Watch and a young priest, Father Tomasz.

sides.name: The Free Assembly
sides.about: Varenne's people in Lyon: the presses, their runners and the silk-weavers they stir up. Green and black.

objectives.text: Find the Assembly's printing houses and close them: {closed} of 4. They look like any other house until your men come close.
The city's temper: {temper} of 20. Every runner who reaches a square raises it; at 20 the city rises.
Father Tomasz speaks to the weavers: he stays on the square by the Weavers' Hall for 45 seconds.
Find the great press under the hill: the traboules lead into its yard.
Take Master Rouvière, the printer, ALIVE: wear him down, then a man of yours beside him.
Raise the city: walk your runners to the squares. The temper {temper} of 20.
Or silence the priest: Father Tomasz.

k_open1.text: The year after Virginia, the Assembly's pamphlets were in every city of the Crown.

k_open2.text: Most of them were printed in Lyon. The Cardinal was there. He was a young priest then.

c_open.text: I was ordained that spring and sent to a parish on the hill. I thought I would baptise silk-weavers' children.

t_open1.text: The papers were on every church door by morning. Nobody saw who nailed them.

t_open_saved.text: The Hollins boys wrote to me from Virginia. Their families were safe. I kept the letter in my breviary.

t_open_left.text: I still prayed for the families we left on the road in Virginia. Nobody wrote to me about them.

t_open2.text: Captain Delorme came to the presbytery. He said: Father, you know these streets. Help me find the presses.

k_open_a.text: The Assembly kept no record of that spring. Here is what it would have done, if it could.

d_1.text: Six presses at least, Father, hidden in houses like any other. The runners carry the papers to the squares.

t_1.text: Then we watch the squares, and follow the runners home.

tip_1.text: A press looks like a house until our men stand at its door. Every runner who reaches a square stirs the city.

tip_2.text: The riders are quick through the streets. Send them to look. Keep the muskets on the squares.

tip_powder.text: Ten shots a musket, Father, then the bayonet. The powder wagon fills them again: keep it near the men.

t_saved.text: In Virginia we saved the families. Here, too, it is the people we must save, not only the walls.

t_left.text: In Virginia we left the families on the road. I will not leave this city to the fire.

w_runner.text: A runner, Captain! A boy with a bundle of papers, running for the squares.

w_hint.text: We saw where a runner came out, Captain. That house there. The door was still open.

d_found.text: A press! Their men are inside. Break it.

t_found.text: Spare the boys who carry the papers if you can. They cannot read what they carry.

d_closed.text: One press silent. The type goes into the river.

t_sermon.text: I spoke on the square until my voice went. Some of them listened. Some went home.

n_temper10.text: Shutters close on the Presqu'île. Men gather at the corners and do not talk when soldiers pass.

n_temper15.text: Stones are thrown at the Watch on the bridges. The city is close to rising.

d_temper15.text: Father, they are close to the edge. Stop the runners or we lose the city.

d_2.text: Four presses closed. Now the Assembly calls the weavers up the hill, to their hall.

t_2.text: Let me speak to them, Captain. They are my parish. Hold the stairs and give me the time.

tip_3.text: Father Tomasz must stand on the hall's square. While he is not there, the agitators turn the weavers.

d_band1.text: A band at the Terreaux, coming up the middle stair!

d_band2.text: More from the Saône bridge, for the west stair.

d_band3.text: And from the Rhône, with torches, for the east stair.

n_turn.text: Weavers pick up stones. A few of them follow the green cockades.

t_turn.text: Bring me to them. They will not turn while I am speaking.

t_spoken.text: I told them who I was, and whose son. I told them nobody in that hall had ever printed bread.

wv_spoken.text: Go home, all of you. The young Father is right. Go home.

n_hall.text: The Weavers' Hall is burning. The whole hill can see it.

wv_yard.text: Father. There is a yard under the hill with no street to it. You go in through the houses.

t_3.text: The traboules. Captain, the great press is there.

tip_4.text: Two passages lead into that yard. Take the printer alive: the King will want to know who pays him.

d_great.text: There it is. A press as big as a church organ.

pr_1.text: You are too late, Father. Half of France has read us already.

d_early.text: A great press in a yard! We will come back for it with more men.

pr_taken.text: Take me, then. The paper is made in Paris. So is everything else.

t_taken.text: He said Paris. He said it as if it were a threat.

d_won.text: The great press is broken. Lyon is quiet.

t_won.text: The bells rang for Lauds. I had not slept, and I said Mass anyway.

d_hurt.text: The Father is hurt! Men round the priest!

n_risen.text: Lyon rises. The Assembly's flags are on the Terreaux.

a_1.text: Your presses print in houses like any other. Walk the runners to the squares and the city will rise.

a_tip.text: The Crown cannot touch a press it has not found. Keep its men away from your doors.

a_layout_old_town.text: Your presses: the hill's west, the slopes, the Presqu'île, Vieux Lyon's north and Guillotière's south.

a_layout_river.text: Your presses: the hill's east, the slopes, the Presqu'île, Vieux Lyon's south and Guillotière's north.

a_layout_hill.text: Your presses: the hill's west, the slopes, the Presqu'île, Vieux Lyon's north and Guillotière's north.

t_end1.text: Rouvière went to Rome in chains. He never said who paid him. He said Paris, again and again.

t_end_calm.text: By Pentecost the weavers were back at their looms, and they came to Mass.

t_end_sullen.text: The city stayed quiet. Quiet is not the same as calm. I heard them stop talking when I passed.

t_end_saved.text: I wrote to the Hollins boys that summer. I told them about Lyon. I did not tell them everything.

c_end.text: I was proud of that spring. I am still. I was also lucky.

k_end1.text: He was more than lucky. He made a city go home without a volley.

k_end_a1.text: That is not how it went. Lyon did not rise.

k_end_a2.text: But if it had, Paris would have had a sister. I have thought of that.

new_horse_breeder.text: NEW: THE HORSE BREEDER. It raises the horses: a mounted man is the fastest thing in a city.

new_cuirassier.text: NEW: THE HORSEMAN. Fast and hard-hitting: ride down the runners before they reach the squares.

text: Lyon, spring 2768. The Free Assembly prints its pamphlets in houses like any other, and its runners carry them to the squares.
Find the printing houses and close them; keep the runners off the squares before the city's temper boils over.
Lyon, spring 2768. You are the Free Assembly. Six of your presses print in the city's houses.
Walk your runners to the squares until the city rises, or silence the young priest.

crown.title: The presses are silent
crown.text: Master Rouvière is taken and the great press broken. Lyon went home.

text_if.text: The city is calm: its temper {temper} of 20.
The city is sullen: its temper {temper} of 20.
{weavers} weavers followed the Assembly on the hill.

assembly.title: Lyon rises
assembly.text: The Assembly's flags fly on the Terreaux. The garrison holds only the east bank.
